stimuli.text: The temperature of a liquid, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by a differentiable function $$H$$ of time $$t$$, in minutes. Selected values are shown.
Water flows into a tank at a rate of $$R(t)$$ gallons per minute, where $$R$$ is a continuous function of time $$t$$ in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The function $$f$$ is continuous on the closed interval $$[0, 4]$$. Selected values of $$f$$ are shown in the table.
The graph of the function $$f$$ shown consists of line segments on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$.

image.alt: Graph of f: line segments through the points (0, -2), (1, -3), (2, 3), (3, 1), (4, -2), (5, 1), (6, -2).

stimuli.text: The graph of $$f'$$, the derivative of a function $$f$$, consists of line segments on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$, as shown.

image.alt: Graph of f′: line segments through the points (0, 2), (1, -1), (2, 0), (3, -3), (4, -1), (5, 3), (6, -1).

image.alt: A slope field drawn on the grid from x = -2 to 2 and y = -2 to 2.

stimuli.text: Water enters a tank at a rate modeled by $$E(t) = 11 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)$$ gallons per hour and leaves the tank at a rate modeled by $$L(t) = 5\sqrt{t + 1}$$ gallons per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the tank contains 96 gallons of water.
Let $$R$$ be the region enclosed by the graphs of $$f(x) = 3\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$g(x) = x^2 - 2$$.
A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $$v(t) = 3t^{2} - 18t + 24$$ for $$t \geq 0$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the particle is at $$x = -2$$.
Consider the curve given by $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 48$$.
People enter an amusement park at a rate modeled by a differentiable function $$P$$, where $$P(t)$$ is measured in people per minute and $$t$$ is measured in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The continuous function $$f$$ is defined on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Its graph consists of line segments, as shown. Let $$g(x) = \int_{2}^{x} f(t)\,dt$$.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of change of $$H$$ over the interval $$5 \leq t \leq 10$$, in degrees Celsius per minute?

options.why: This is the total change in temperature; it still needs to be divided by the elapsed time.
This is the average temperature, not the average rate of change.
This divides time by temperature, which is upside down.

questions.explanation: Average rate of change $$= \frac{H(10) - H(5)}{10 - 5} = \frac{20 - 44}{5} = -\frac{24}{5}$$ degrees per minute.

options.why: This is $$f'(2)$$, the first derivative.
This drops the constant that comes from the quadratic term.
This lowers each exponent twice but only multiplies by the exponent once.

questions.stem: Using the line tangent to $$f(x) = \sqrt{x}$$ at $$x = 36$$, what is the approximation of $$\sqrt{37}$$?

options.why: The derivative of $$\sqrt{x}$$ is $$\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$$; this forgets the 2.
Sign error: the change in x is added, not subtracted.
This uses slope $$\frac{1}{2}$$ instead of $$f'(36) = \frac{1}{12}$$.

questions.stem: Using a left Riemann sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table, what is the approximation of $$\int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt$$?

options.why: This is the right Riemann sum.
This treats every subinterval as width 2, but the subintervals have unequal widths.
Correct. Multiply each subinterval's width by the appropriate height and add.
This is the trapezoidal sum.

questions.explanation: The widths are 2, 1, 4, 3. Use the left endpoint of each subinterval, multiply by the width and add: $$47$$ gallons.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} - 24x^{2} + 72x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative maximum?

options.why: $$f(0) = 0$$, but $$f'(0)$$ is not zero, so this is not a critical point.
At this critical point $$f'$$ changes from negative to positive, which gives a relative minimum.
Correct. $$f'(x) = 6(x - 2)(x - 6)$$ changes from positive to negative at $$x = 2$$.
This is where f″ = 0 (the inflection point), not a critical point.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 6x^2 - 48x + 72 = 6(x - 2)(x - 6)$$. Testing signs: $$f'$$ is positive left of $$2$$, negative between $$2$$ and $$6$$, positive right of $$6$$. So there is a relative maximum at $$2$$ and a relative minimum at $$6$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time $$t \geq 0$$ is $$x(t) = t^{3} - 9t^{2} + 24t$$. At what times is the particle at rest?

options.why: Correct. $$v(t) = 3t^2 - 18t + 24 = 3(t - 2)(t - 4)$$, which is zero at $$t = 2$$ and $$t = 4$$.
This is where the position is zero, not the velocity.
At $$t = 0$$ the position is 0, but the velocity is $$24$$, so the particle is moving.
This is where the acceleration is zero, not the velocity.

questions.explanation: The particle is at rest when $$v(t) = x'(t) = 0$$. $$v(t) = 3(t - 2)(t - 4)$$, so $$t = 2$$ and $$t = 4$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_{1}^{3} \left(6x^{2} - 2x + 5\right)dx$$?

options.why: Correct. An antiderivative is $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - x^{2} + 5x$$; $$F(3) - F(1) = 54$$.
This is F(b) only; subtract F(a) as well.
This adds F(a) instead of subtracting it.
This subtracts values of the integrand instead of an antiderivative.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx = F(3) - F(1)$$ with $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - x^{2} + 5x$$. That is $$60 - (6) = 54$$.

questions.stem: Let $$C(x)$$ be the cost, in dollars, of producing x items. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$C'(3) = 5$$?

options.text: The cost when 3 items have been produced is 5.
options.why: This describes $$C(3)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The average rate of change of the cost over the first 3 items is 5 dollars per item.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The cost is increasing at a rate of 5 dollars per item when 3 items have been produced.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

options.text: The cost changes by 5 over the first 3 items.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

questions.explanation: $$C'(3)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$C$$ when 3 items have been produced. Its sign (positive) says the cost is increasing, and its units are dollars per item.

options.why: This applies the power rule to the derivative of the inside instead of to the inside function.
This is the value of the function, not its derivative.
This differentiates the outer power but leaves out the derivative of the inside function.

questions.stem: A twice-differentiable function $$f$$ satisfies $$f'(-1) = 0$$ and $$f''(-1) = 0$$. Which of the following must be true?

options.text: $$f$$ has a point of inflection at $$x = -1$$.
options.why: $$x^3$$ has an inflection point there, but $$x^4$$ does not.
$$x^4$$ has a minimum, but $$-x^4$$ has a maximum with the same conditions.
$$-x^4$$ has a maximum, but $$x^4$$ has a minimum with the same conditions.

options.text: There is not enough information to classify $$x = -1$$.
options.why: Correct. When f″(c) = 0 the Second Derivative Test is inconclusive: $$x^3$$, $$x^4$$ and $$-x^4$$ all have f′(0) = f″(0) = 0.

questions.explanation: With $$f''(c) = 0$$ the test gives no conclusion. Use the First Derivative Test instead.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{6} \frac{1}{x + 3}\,dx$$?

options.why: This uses a power-rule-style antiderivative; the antiderivative of 1/u is ln|u|.
Correct. $$\ln|x + 3|\Big|_0^{6} = \ln 9 - \ln 3 = \ln 3$$.
This forgets to subtract the value at the lower limit.
This is the ratio minus one, not a logarithm.

questions.explanation: $$\int \frac{dx}{x + 3} = \ln|x + 3| + C$$, so the integral is $$\ln\frac{9}{3} = \ln 3$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to -1} \frac{x^{2} - x - 2}{x + 1}$$?

options.why: Correct. The numerator factors as $$(x + 1)(x - 2)$$. Cancel $$x + 1$$ and substitute: $$-1 - (2) = -3$$.
The expression is undefined at the point, but its outputs nearby approach a single number, so the limit exists.
This adds the roots. After cancelling, the expression is $$x - 2$$, which approaches $$-3$$.
Substituting gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form, not the value 0.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so factor: $$x^{2} - x - 2 = (x + 1)(x - 2)$$. For $$x \neq -1$$ the expression equals $$x - 2$$, so the limit is $$-1 - (2) = -3$$.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y$$ with $$f(1) = -3$$. Using the tangent line at $$x = 1$$, what is the approximation of $$f(1.1)$$?

options.why: This adds the slope without multiplying by the step 0.1.
This is only the estimated change; add it to f(a).
Sign error in the step.

questions.explanation: At $$(1, -3)$$, $$\frac{dy}{dx} = -2$$. The tangent line gives $$f(1.1) \approx -3 + (-2)(0.1) = -3.2$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of $$f(x) = x^{2} + 4x - 5$$ at $$x = -1$$?

options.why: This uses the function value $$-8$$ as the slope.
This slope drops the derivative of $$4x$$.
This swaps the x- and y-coordinates of the point of tangency.
Correct. The point is $$(-1, -8)$$ and the slope is $$f'(-1) = 2$$.
The derivative of $$e^x$$ is $$e^x$$, which equals $$e$$ at 1, not 1.
This uses $$\ln 1 = 0$$, but the derivative of $$\ln x$$ is $$\frac{1}{x}$$, which is 1 at $$x = 1$$.
The derivative of $$-x^2$$ is $$-2x$$.

questions.explanation: Differentiate term by term: $$f'(x) = 5e^{x} + \frac{3}{x} - 2x$$. At $$x = 1$$ this is $$5e + 1$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}$$ with $$y(0) = 3$$?

options.why: At $$x = 0$$ this gives $$\sqrt{3}$$, not $$3$$: the constant must be $$3^2$$.
The initial value is positive, so the positive root is needed.
Correct. $$y\,dy = x\,dx$$ gives $$y^2 = x^2 + C$$; $$C = 9$$, and the positive root matches $$y(0) = 3$$.
This would have dy/dx = 1, which is not x/y.

questions.explanation: Separate: $$\int y\,dy = \int x\,dx$$, so $$\frac{y^2}{2} = \frac{x^2}{2} + C$$. With $$y(0) = 3$$, $$y^2 = x^2 + 9$$ and $$y = \sqrt{x^2 + 9}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{3} + 4x$$, and let $$g$$ be the inverse function of $$f$$. What is $$g'(-5)$$?

options.why: This takes the reciprocal of a function value, not of the derivative.
This is $$f'(-1)$$; the inverse's derivative is its reciprocal.
This evaluates $$f'$$ at $$-5$$ instead of at the input $$-1$$ with $$f(-1) = -5$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 2 & x \leq 3 \\ 6x - 11 & x > 3 \end{cases}$$. Which of the following is true?

options.text: $$f$$ is continuous but not differentiable at $$x = 3$$.
options.why: The one-sided slopes match, so there is no corner.

options.text: $$f$$ is differentiable but not continuous at $$x = 3$$.
options.why: Differentiability implies continuity, so this can never happen.
Correct. The left piece gives $$f(3) = 7$$ with slope $$6$$; the right piece approaches $$7$$ with slope $$6$$. The values and the slopes both match.

options.text: $$f$$ is neither continuous nor differentiable at $$x = 3$$.
options.why: The one-sided limits match, so $$f$$ is continuous.

questions.explanation: The left piece gives $$f(3) = 7$$ with slope $$6$$; the right piece approaches $$7$$ with slope $$6$$. Matching values give continuity, and matching one-sided derivatives give differentiability.

questions.stem: The derivative of a function $$f$$ is $$f'(x) = (x + 2)^2x$$. On which intervals is $$f$$ increasing?

options.why: On $$-2 < x < 0$$ the factor $$x$$ is negative.
Here f′ < 0 because $$x < 0$$.
Correct. The squared factor is never negative, so the sign of $$f'$$ matches $$x$$.
The squared factor does not change sign at $$x = -2$$, so f′ < 0 for $$x < -2$$.

questions.explanation: $$(x + 2)^2 \geq 0$$ for all $$x$$, so $$f'(x) > 0$$ exactly when $$x > 0$$. Note $$f'$$ does not change sign at $$-2$$, so there is no extremum there.

questions.stem: The base of a solid is the region bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}$$, the x-axis, and $$x = 4$$. Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are semicircles. What is the volume of the solid?

options.why: This is the volume for cross sections that are equilateral triangles.
This is the volume for cross sections that are squares.
This is the volume for cross sections that are isosceles right triangles with a leg in the base.
Correct. Each cross section has diameter $$\sqrt{x}$$, area $$\frac{\pi}{8}x$$; integrate from 0 to 4.

questions.explanation: The cross section at $x$ has diameter $$\sqrt{x}$$, area $$\frac{\pi}{8}x$$. Integrating from 0 to 4 gives $\pi$.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sqrt{x + 16} - 4}{x}$$?

options.why: This forgets that the conjugate denominator is $$\sqrt{x + 16} + 4$$, which approaches $$8$$, not $$4$$.
Correct. Rationalizing gives $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 16} + 4}$$, which approaches $$\frac{1}{8}$$.
The expression is undefined at 0, but rationalizing shows the outputs approach a single number.
Substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form.

questions.explanation: Multiply by $$\frac{\sqrt{x + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x + 16} + 4}$$. The numerator becomes $$x$$, which cancels, leaving $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 16} + 4} \to \frac{1}{8}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \frac{x^{2} + 4x - 5}{x^{2} + 3x - 10}$$. Which of the following lists every vertical asymptote of the graph of $$f$$?

options.why: Correct. The factor $$x + 5$$ cancels, leaving a hole at $$x = -5$$. Only $$x = 2$$ makes the simplified denominator zero.
At $$x = -5$$ the numerator is also zero; the common factor cancels, giving a removable discontinuity (a hole), not an asymptote.
$$x = -5$$ is a hole, because its factor cancels.
$$x = 1$$ is a zero of the numerator, so it is an x-intercept, not an asymptote.

questions.explanation: Factor: $$f(x) = \frac{(x + 5)(x - 1)}{(x + 5)(x - 2)}$$. The common factor gives a hole at $$x = -5$$; near $$x = 2$$ the denominator approaches 0 while the numerator does not, so $$x = 2$$ is the only vertical asymptote.

questions.stem: The region bounded by $$y = x^2$$, the x-axis, and the line $$x = 1$$ is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the resulting solid?

options.why: The disc method has a factor of $$\pi$$.
$$(x^2)^2 = x^4$$, whose antiderivative is $$\frac{x^5}{5}$$.
This integrates the radius instead of the radius squared.

questions.stem: What is the least number of solutions that the equation $$f(x) = 0$$ must have on the interval $$[0, 4]$$?

options.why: This undercounts: each sign change between consecutive values guarantees its own zero.
Correct. The sign of $$f$$ changes 1 time between consecutive table values, and the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a zero in each such interval.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.

questions.explanation: Because $$f$$ is continuous, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a solution of $$f(x) = 0$$ on every interval where the values change sign. Counting the sign changes in the table gives 1.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{0}^{5} f(x)\,dx$$?

options.why: This is f(b) − f(a), the change in f, not the integral of f.
This is the total area, treating regions below the axis as positive.
Correct. Add the areas above the x-axis and subtract the areas below it.
Sign error: regions above the axis count positive.

questions.explanation: Split $$[0, 5]$$ into unit intervals and add the signed areas of the trapezoids and triangles: the result is $$-\frac{3}{2}$$.

options.why: You cannot integrate a quotient by integrating the top and bottom separately.
The antiderivative of $$\frac{1}{x}$$ is $$\ln|x|$$.
The antiderivative of $$3x$$ is $$\frac{3}{2}x^2$$.
Correct. Divide first: $$\frac{3x^{2} - 5}{x} = 3x + \frac{-5}{x}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int \left(3x + \frac{-5}{x}\right)dx = \frac{3}{2}x^2 - 5\ln|x| + C$$.

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \arctan(2x)$$, what is $$f'(2)$$?

options.why: This uses $$1 + x^2$$ in the denominator instead of $$1 + (2x)^2$$.
This leaves out the inner derivative $$2$$.
The inside is squared as a whole: $$(2x)^2 = 4x^2$$.
Correct. $$f'(x) = \frac{2}{1 + 4x^2}$$.

questions.stem: On which of the following intervals is the graph of $$f$$ concave down?

options.why: Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.
Correct. $$f'$$ is decreasing there, so $$f'' < 0$$.
Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.
Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.

questions.explanation: $$f$$ is concave down where $$f'$$ is decreasing, which on this graph means a segment sloping downward.

questions.stem: An open-top box is made from a 18-inch by 18-inch square of cardboard by cutting equal squares of side $$x$$ from each corner and folding up the sides. What value of $$x$$ gives the box its maximum volume?

options.why: This is not a critical point of the volume.
This is not a critical point of the volume.
At this cut the base has zero width, which gives volume 0 (a minimum).

questions.explanation: $$V'(x) = (18 - 2x)^2 - 4x(18 - 2x) = (18 - 2x)(18 - 6x)$$. On $$0 < x < 9$$, the only critical point is $$x = 3$$, where $$V'$$ changes from positive to negative.

questions.stem: Let $$R$$ be the region bounded by $$y = x^2$$ and $$y = 1$$. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when $$R$$ is revolved about the line $$y = 1$$?

options.why: The radius must be squared, and the region runs from −k to k.
Correct. Each disc has radius $$1 - x^2$$, the distance from the curve to the axis.
This is the washer formula for revolving about the x-axis.
This uses the distance from the curve to the x-axis, not to the line of revolution.

questions.explanation: Revolving about $$y = 1$$, which is the top boundary, gives discs of radius $$1 - x^2$$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{0}^{2} \frac{x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx$$?

options.why: This integrates over only half of the interval.
Correct. Use the calculator's numerical integration.
This is the change in the integrand, not the integral.
This is a single rectangle using the right endpoint, a rough estimate rather than the integral.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, $$\int_{0}^{2} \frac{x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx \approx 1.717$$.

questions.stem: $$\int \left(5x^{4} + 1\cdot\frac{1}{x} + 5e^{x}\right)dx =$$

options.why: Correct. Raise the power by one and divide by the new power; the antiderivative of 1/x is ln|x|; e^x is its own antiderivative.
After raising the power, divide by the new exponent.
This differentiates instead of antidifferentiating.
The antiderivative of 1/x is ln|x|, not a power of x.

questions.explanation: Term by term: $$\int 5x^{4}dx = x^{5}$$, $$\int \frac{1}{x}dx = \ln|x|$$, and $$\int 5e^x dx = 5e^x$$. Add the constant of integration.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{2} - 4x$$. What value of $$c$$ satisfies the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem for $$f$$ on the interval $$[-3, 1]$$?

options.why: This is where f′(c) = 0, the vertex, not where f′(c) equals the average rate of change.
The MVT guarantees a point strictly inside the interval, and this endpoint doesn't satisfy the equation.
Correct. The average rate of change is $$\frac{f(1) - f(-3)}{4} = -6$$, and $$f'(c) = 2c - 4 = -6$$ gives $$c = -1$$.
The MVT guarantees a point strictly inside the interval, and this endpoint doesn't satisfy the equation.

questions.stem: Which of the following differential equations could have the slope field shown?

options.why: Test a few points: at some grid points this equation gives a slope with the wrong sign or steepness.
Test a few points: at some grid points this equation gives a slope with the wrong sign or steepness.
Correct. Check where the segments are horizontal and where the slopes are positive or negative; this equation matches at every point.
Test a few points: at some grid points this equation gives a slope with the wrong sign or steepness.

questions.explanation: Compare slopes at specific points. For example, at $$(1, 0)$$ the field's segment has slope $$1$$, and at $$(0, 1)$$ slope $$0$$, which matches $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2$$.

questions.stem: The function $$g$$ is defined by $$g(x) = \frac{\sin(5x)}{e^{2x} - 1}$$ for $$x \neq 0$$. For what value of $$g(0)$$ is $$g$$ continuous at $$x = 0$$?

options.why: Substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, which is indeterminate, not 0.
Correct. Evaluating $$g$$ at inputs very close to 0 (or using the limits of $$\frac{\sin u}{u}$$ and $$\frac{e^u - 1}{u}$$) gives $$\frac{5}{2}$$.
The two small quantities do not shrink at the same rate.
This inverts the ratio.

questions.explanation: For continuity, $$g(0)$$ must equal $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x)$$. Near 0, $$\sin(5x) \approx 5x$$ and $$e^{2x} - 1 \approx 2x$$, so the limit is $$\frac{5}{2} \approx 2.500$$. A table of values near 0 confirms it.

questions.stem: What is the area of the region enclosed by the graphs of $$y = 4\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$y = x^2 - 1$$?

options.why: This is the distance between the intersection points, not an area.
Correct. The curves meet at $$x \approx -1.847$$ and $$x \approx 1.847$$; integrate top minus bottom.
This is the area under the top curve only.
This adds the absolute values of the curves instead of subtracting.

questions.explanation: Store the intersection x-values from the calculator, then $$\int_{-1.847}^{1.847} \left(4\cos\frac{x}{2} - (x^2 - 1)\right)dx \approx 12.257$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \sqrt{x}\,\cos x$$. What is the value of $$f'(2)$$?

options.why: This multiplies the derivatives of the factors instead of using the product rule.
This is the derivative at $$x = 3$$, not at $$x = 2$$.
Correct. Use the calculator's numerical derivative (or the correct rule) at the given input.
This is the function value, not the derivative.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, evaluate $$\left.\frac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt{x}\,\cos x\right)\right|_{x = 2} \approx -1.433$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $$v(t) = 4\cos\left(\frac{t^2}{5}\right) - 0.5$$ for $$0 \leq t \leq 3$$. At what time does the particle first change direction?

options.why: This is the initial velocity, not a time.
Correct. The velocity first changes sign at $$t \approx 2.688$$, found by solving $$v(t) = 0$$ on the calculator.
This is a later time; the question asks for the first change of direction.
This is an acceleration value, not a time when the velocity changes sign.

questions.explanation: A particle changes direction where $$v(t)$$ changes sign. Graphing $$v$$ on the calculator, the first sign change is at $$t \approx 2.688$$.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = x^2e^{-x/3} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 7]$$?

options.why: This is where the maximum occurs (the x-value), not the maximum value.
This is the value at the right endpoint, which is not the largest.
Correct. Graph f on the calculator and find its maximum on the interval, checking the endpoints too.
This evaluates f at the critical point of the first term alone; the sine term shifts the maximum.

questions.explanation: On the calculator, the maximum of $$f$$ on $$[0, 7]$$ occurs at $$x \approx 6.889$$, where $$f(x) \approx 4.918$$. The endpoint values are smaller.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 57 + 5\sin\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 13$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

options.why: This is the temperature itself, not its rate of change.
Correct. The calculator's numerical derivative of $$H$$ at $$t = 13$$ gives -0.231; the temperature is decreasing.
This is the average rate of change over $$0 \leq t \leq 13$$, not the instantaneous rate.
This multiplies the rate by the time, which is not a rate.

questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change is $$H'(13) \approx -0.231$$ degrees Fahrenheit per hour, from the calculator's numerical derivative.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 2\sin(t)\,e^{-t/6} + 0.3$$. What is the total distance the particle travels over $$0 \leq t \leq 5$$?

options.why: This is the displacement; backward motion subtracts from it.
This is the average speed, not the distance.
Correct. $$\int_0^{5} |v(t)|\,dt$$ on the calculator.
This is the speed at the final time.

questions.explanation: Total distance $$= \int_0^{5} |v(t)|\,dt \approx 4.820$$. The displacement $$\int_0^{5} v(t)\,dt \approx 3.341$$ is smaller because the particle moves backward part of the time.

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 29 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 7$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 224 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 7$$?

options.why: This adds the rate at one instant, not the accumulated amount.
Correct. $$224 + \int_0^{7} R(t)\,dt$$.
This is only the sand added; include the initial amount.
